title: Follow-up, left knee after meniscus repair, stairs still hard

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Good morning. How has the left knee been since our last visit?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Better on flat ground. The pain is about 4/10 most days, but stairs are still hard.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Have you been doing the home exercises?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I did the home exercises five days out of seven. I skipped the wall sits because they hurt.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Any numbness, tingling or night pain?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No numbness or tingling, and no night pain.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: I measured knee flexion at 95 degrees today, up from 85 degrees two weeks ago.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Quadriceps strength is 4/5 on the left and 5/5 on the right.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My goal is to walk my daughter to school without stopping.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: My assessment is that range of motion is improving and the remaining limit is quadriceps strength.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Plan: continue the home program, replace wall sits with step-ups, and follow up in two weeks.

expectedFacts.statement: Home exercises five of seven days, wall sits skipped
Range of motion improving, strength is the limit

notes: WP 5.1 fixture. Every missing-information item is covered.
